## 1. Repository structure, language, tooling, and where the change would land

**Stack:** Rust workspace (edition 2021, ~45 crates under `lib/apps`, `lib/components`, `lib/foundation`, plus `test/twin/*` test doubles), one React 19/Bun web app (`apps/fabro-web`), a generated TS Axios client (`lib/packages/fabro-api-client`), and Mintlify docs (`docs/public`). Testing: `cargo nextest`, insta snapshots, dual-mode e2e tests, and a **twin GitHub server** (`test/twin/github`) that emulates the GitHub API surface (app/installations/tokens, OAuth, pulls, branches, releases, GraphQL, git smart-HTTP) for tests. OpenAPI spec `docs/public/api-reference/fabro-api.yaml` is the wire source of truth (progenitor → Rust, openapi-generator → TS).

**"GitHub integration" is not one module — it's a vertical slice through ~8 crates, 6 direct dependents of `fabro-github`:**

| Layer | File(s) | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| API client crate | `lib/components/fabro-github/` (`lib.rs` 2948 L, `access.rs`, `token_source.rs`) | GitHub App JWT (RS256), installation-token minting, PAT, `HttpClient` trait + mocks, PR create/get/merge/close/auto-merge, branch head SHA, clone-credential embedding (`x-access-token` URL), owner/repo URL parsing, git credential-helper (`GITHUB_TOKEN`), webhook config update, `gh auth token` |
| Types | `lib/foundation/fabro-types/` | `GitHubRepositorySlug`, `RepositoryProvider::{Github,Git,Unknown}`, `PullRequestLink` (hard-requires `https://github.com/.../pull/N`), `PullRequestGithubDetail`, `RunIntent` git-target validation ("repository must be a valid GitHub owner/name slug"), settings: `[server.integrations.github]` (token/app strategy), `[server.auth.github]` (OAuth login), `[run.integrations.github]` (runtime `GITHUB_TOKEN` minting w/ permissions + `additional_repositories`), `RunScmSettings { provider, owner, repository, github }` (provider currently a free string), `IntegrationProvider::{Github,Slack}` |
| Server | `lib/apps/fabro-server/` | `github_webhooks.rs` (`POST /api/v1/webhooks/github`, HMAC `X-Hub-Signature-256`), `auth/github_endpoints.rs` (browser OAuth login), `system.rs` handler (`/api/v1/repos/github/{owner}/{name}` preflight, `/install/github/*` wizard routes), `diagnostics.rs` (connectivity checks), `automation_materializer.rs` (webhook → run automations), `run_manifest.rs` (run admission: GitHub-only origin parsing, clone probes, credential resolution) |
| Sandbox | `lib/components/fabro-sandbox/` | `clone_source.rs` (**"Clone-based sandboxes currently support GitHub repository origins only"** — Docker/Daytona clone layout `repos/<owner>/<repo>`), `push_credentials.rs`, `docker.rs`, `daytona/` (SDK clone by owner/repo), `git_retry.rs` (token-replication-lag handling) |
| Workflow | `lib/components/fabro-workflow/` | PR pipeline (`pipeline/pull_request.rs`: LLM-generated title/body, PR create/merge via `GitHubContext`), `git_bridge.rs` (credential helper), `pipeline/initialize.rs` (mints run `GITHUB_TOKEN` from `GitHubRepositoryAccess`), token refresh/provenance threading |
| Tracker | `lib/components/fabro-tracker/src/github.rs` | GitHub Projects V2 via GraphQL |
| Install/onboarding | `lib/components/fabro-install/`, `fabro-cli/src/commands/install.rs` | `fabro install github` (token or App strategy; App-manifest registration flow), vault secrets `GITHUB_TOKEN`, `GITHUB_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`, `GITHUB_APP_CLIENT_SECRET`, `GITHUB_APP_WEBHOOK_SECRET` |
| CLI extras | `fabro-cli/src/gh.rs` | best-effort `gh` CLI detection |
| Tests/docs | `test/twin/github`, `docs/public/integrations/github.mdx`, `docs.json` nav, OpenAPI schemas, `.env.example`, web app `settings-integrations.tsx` / `auth-login.tsx` / install wizard | full GitHub-shaped surfaces |

A new Forgejo integration would most naturally land as a **new component crate (e.g. `fabro-forgejo`)** mirroring `fabro-github`, plus touches in types, settings, server, sandbox, workflow, tracker, install, CLI, OpenAPI, twin-tests, and docs — or alternatively as a **provider abstraction** extracted under the existing `scm` config concept.

## 2. Goal restated, concretely

> Let Fabro operate against a **self-hosted Forgejo instance** (a Gitea fork; API at `<instance>/api/v1`) the way it operates against GitHub today: a user can configure Forgejo credentials in settings/vault, run workflows whose git origin points at the Forgejo instance (clone-based Docker/Daytona sandboxes accept it), get per-run tokens injected, have runs open/merge/close pull requests on Forgejo, optionally receive Forgejo webhooks to trigger automations, and manage connection status/diagnostics from the web UI — with docs and tests mirroring `docs/public/integrations/github.mdx` and `test/twin/github`.

Forgejo platform facts I verified against current docs: API base is `<instance>/api/v1` (self-hosted, must be configurable); auth is PAT (`Authorization: token ...`), OAuth2 tokens (`Bearer ...`), or basic auth — **there is no GitHub-App-style RS256-JWT → installation-token endpoint**; "Authorized Integrations" (JWT/OIDC, JWKS-validated) exist but target CI-issued tokens, not a hosted server minting scoped tokens. REST endpoints are Gitea-shaped (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`, merge via `POST .../pulls/{index}/merge` with `Do` field) — *not* byte-identical to GitHub (different paths, methods, payload field names, pagination).

## 3. What I now know for certain

- The integration is **deep and load-bearing**: `fabro-github` has 6 dependent crates; origin parsing, run admission, sandbox cloning, PR lifecycle, token minting/refresh (with provenance and replication-lag retry), webhooks, OAuth login, install wizard, diagnostics, and system-integration status are all GitHub-specific today.
- There is an **existing seam for multi-SCM**: `RunScmSettings { provider: Option<String>, owner, repository, github: Option<ScmGitHubSettings> }` in run settings (also in the OpenAPI spec), and `RepositoryProvider::{Github, Git, Unknown}` — i.e., the codebase already anticipates named SCM providers even though everything below it assumes GitHub.
- `GITHUB_BASE_URL` env override already exists in `fabro-github::github_api_base_url()` (used by tests/diagnostics) — but the URL grammar (`parse_github_owner_repo`) is hard-coded to `github.com` hostnames, so it alone can't target a Forgejo instance.
- Clone-based providers (Docker, Daytona) **explicitly reject non-GitHub origins** (`clone_source.rs` error message; CLAUDE.md documents "GitHub-only clone-source contract"). Daytona clones via its SDK with `owner/repo` + GitHub credentials.

Forgejo platform facts I verified against current docs: API base is `<instance>/api/v1` (self-hosted, must be configurable); auth is PAT (`Authorization: token ...`), OAuth2 tokens (`Bearer ...`), or basic auth — **there is no GitHub-App-style RS256-JWT → installation-token endpoint**; "Authorized Integrations" (JWT/OIDC, JWKS-validated) exist but target CI-issued tokens, not a hosted server minting scoped tokens. REST endpoints are Gitea-shaped (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`, merge via `POST .../pulls/{index}/merge` with `Do` field) — *not* byte-identical to GitHub (different paths, methods, payload field names, pagination).

## 3. What I now know for certain

- The integration is **deep and load-bearing**: `fabro-github` has 6 dependent crates; origin parsing, run admission, sandbox cloning, PR lifecycle, token minting/refresh (with provenance and replication-lag retry), webhooks, OAuth login, install wizard, diagnostics, and system-integration status are all GitHub-specific today.

- `GITHUB_BASE_URL` env override already exists in `fabro-github::github_api_base_url()` (used by tests/diagnostics) — but the URL grammar (`parse_github_owner_repo`) is hard-coded to `github.com` hostnames, so it alone can't target a Forgejo instance.
- Clone-based providers (Docker, Daytona) **explicitly reject non-GitHub origins** (`clone_source.rs` error message; CLAUDE.md documents "GitHub-only clone-source contract"). Daytona clones via its SDK with `owner/repo` + GitHub credentials.
- Secrets flow: vault-backed (`fabro-install` writes `GITHUB_*` keys), with a registry of secret env names (`fabro-static/src/secret_registry.rs`) and scrubbing policy.
- The test architecture expects a **twin server** per external dependency (`test/twin/openai`, `test/twin/github` with fixture-driven handlers + git smart-HTTP), and strategy docs (`docs/internal/`) constrain events, errors, testing, secrets, migrations, and API type ownership — all apply to this feature.

- Webhook ingestion is one route (`/api/v1/webhooks/github`) authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 `X-Hub-Signature-256`, feeding automations via `automation_materializer.rs`.

- There is an **existing seam for multi-SCM**: `RunScmSettings { provider: Option<String>, owner, repository, github: Option<ScmGitHubSettings> }` in run settings (also in the OpenAPI spec), and `RepositoryProvider::{Github, Git, Unknown}` — i.e., the codebase already anticipates named SCM providers even though everything below it assumes GitHub.
- `GITHUB_BASE_URL` env override already exists in `fabro-github::github_api_base_url()` (used by tests/diagnostics) — but the URL grammar (`parse_github_owner_repo`) is hard-coded to `github.com` hostnames, so it alone can't target a Forgejo instance.
- Clone-based providers (Docker, Daytona) **explicitly reject non-GitHub origins** (`clone_source.rs` error message; CLAUDE.md documents "GitHub-only clone-source contract"). Daytona clones via its SDK with `owner/repo` + GitHub credentials.
- Secrets flow: vault-backed (`fabro-install` writes `GITHUB_*` keys), with a registry of secret env names (`fabro-static/src/secret_registry.rs`) and scrubbing policy.
- The test architecture expects a **twin server** per external dependency (`test/twin/openai`, `test/twin/github` with fixture-driven handlers + git smart-HTTP), and strategy docs (`docs/internal/`) constrain events, errors, testing, secrets, migrations, and API type ownership — all apply to this feature.
- Auth model: browser login via GitHub OAuth (`ServerAuthMethod::Github`, `github_endpoints.rs`, `/login/oauth/*` + `/user`), distinct from the repo-integration credential strategy (`token` vs `app`).
- Webhook ingestion is one route (`/api/v1/webhooks/github`) authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 `X-Hub-Signature-256`, feeding automations via `automation_materializer.rs`.
- Forgejo specifics (from official docs, v16): `/api/v1` base, `token`/`Bearer`/basic auth, OAuth2 provider present, pagination `page`/`limit`, OpenAPI published at `/swagger.v1.json`; no installation-token equivalent.

## 4. Genuinely ambiguous — where two engineers would build different things

1. **Scope of parity.** Full GitHub parity (clone, run token, PRs, webhooks, OAuth login, tracker, install wizard, diagnostics) vs. the pragmatic core (PAT auth + clone + PR lifecycle)? "Similar to github integration" doesn't say. GitHub Projects V2 tracker almost certainly has **no Forgejo equivalent** (Gitea/Forgejo projects lack a public GraphQL API).
2. **Auth model mapping.** GitHub has App (JWT → scoped installation tokens, the basis of `GITHUB_TOKEN` minting and `token_source.rs` refresh logic) vs. PAT. Forgejo only has PAT/OAuth2. Do we: (a) support only a static PAT (simplest; kills the per-run scoped-token feature), (b) map to Forgejo OAuth2 tokens, or (c) attempt "Authorized Integrations" JWT (JWKS-hosting required — Fabro would have to run an OIDC issuer, a big new surface)?
3. **Instance URL model.** One Forgejo instance configured globally (server-level, like `[server.integrations.forgejo] url = "..."`), or resolved per-repo-origin (any host that isn't github.com)? And how do run origins get classified — does `RepositoryProvider` grow a `Forgejo` variant, and is that by configured-instance match or URL heuristics? Affects `GitHubRepositorySlug`, `PullRequestLink` (currently hard-coded to `github.com` URLs), DB-stored data, and the API schema.
4. **Architecture: sibling crate vs. provider abstraction.** A `fabro-forgejo` crate next to `fabro-github` (fast, parallel, but duplicates and pushes `if provider == …` branching into server/workflow/sandbox), vs. extracting a `ForgeProvider` trait (e.g. parse origin / resolve clone creds / create PR / merge PR) that both implement — a large refactor of `fabro-github`'s public surface (`GitHubContext`, `GitHubRepositoryAccess`, `InstallationTokenSource`) that touches every dependent crate. Also: does `token_source.rs`'s refresh/provenance machinery get reused for static Forgejo PATs (it already has a `Static` provenance) or forked?
5. **API-shape translation.** Gitea-family REST differs in details (merge endpoint method/fields like `Do`, token header `token` vs `Bearer`, pagination, PR JSON schema differences feeding `PullRequestGithubDetail`). Do we translate into existing GitHub-shaped types (least churn, risk of semantic drift — e.g. no token expiry, no auto-merge API) or introduce provider-tagged PR detail types? Note CLAUDE.md's rule against `ApiFoo` adapter-smell types cuts both ways here.
6. **Webhooks.** Forgejo/Gitea webhooks use different payload shapes ("gitea" event type) and signature headers (needs verification: `X-Gitea-Signature` vs `X-Hub-Signature-256`, which Forgejo also supports for "github"-type webhooks). New route `/api/v1/webhooks/forgejo`? Separate secret? Does the automation materializer understand both event grammars? Is the Tailscale-funnel/server-URL webhook strategy reused?
7. **OAuth login.** Is "sign in with your Forgejo account" (a *self-hosted* IdP — issuer/allowed-hosts config, trust questions, `AuthMethod`/`IdpIdentity` changes) part of this, or out of scope? Two reasonable answers.
8. **Multi-tenancy.** GitHub is a single global counterparty; Forgejo is many instances. Support exactly one configured instance, or several simultaneously (per-run origin decides)? Changes settings schema, vault keys (`FORGEJO_TOKEN`? per-instance?), and slug identity (owner/repo is no longer unique without the instance).
9. **Non-goals / adjacent providers.** Should the design generalize to Gitea itself (Forgejo is Gitea-compatible; codeberg.org is Forgejo) from day one, or hard-scope to Forgejo branding? `is_github_origin`-style host matching would then be wrong for one of them.
10. **Product surfaces.** Does the web install wizard, `fabro install forgejo` CLI, system integrations status card (`IntegrationProvider::Forgejo`), and OpenAPI/TS client updates all land in phase one, or is this a CLI/server-only feature initially? (The OpenAPI-first workflow makes each schema change ripple into conformance tests and the generated TS client.)

**Recommended clarifications before building:** (1) target scope (clone+PR core vs. full parity), (2) PAT-only auth for v1, (3) single configured instance vs. per-origin detection, (4) sibling crate with a thin shared trait vs. full provider abstraction. Everything else can follow from those four decisions.

## 2. Goal restated, concretely

- Secrets flow: vault-backed (`fabro-install` writes `GITHUB_*` keys), with a registry of secret env names (`fabro-static/src/secret_registry.rs`) and scrubbing policy.
- The test architecture expects a **twin server** per external dependency (`test/twin/openai`, `test/twin/github` with fixture-driven handlers + git smart-HTTP), and strategy docs (`docs/internal/`) constrain events, errors, testing, secrets, migrations, and API type ownership — all apply to this feature.

3. **Instance URL model.** One Forgejo instance configured globally (server-level, like `[server.integrations.forgejo] url = "..."`), or resolved per-repo-origin (any host that isn't github.com)? Affects `GitHubRepositorySlug`, `PullRequestLink` (currently hard-coded to `github.com` URLs), DB-stored data, and the API schema.
4. **Architecture: sibling crate vs. provider abstraction.** A `fabro-forgejo` crate next to `fabro-github` (fast, parallel, but duplicates and pushes `if provider == …` branching into server/workflow/sandbox), vs. extracting a `ForgeProvider` trait (e.g. parse origin / resolve clone creds / create PR / merge PR) that both implement — a large refactor of `fabro-github`'s public surface (`GitHubContext`, `GitHubRepositoryAccess`, `InstallationTokenSource`) that touches every dependent crate. Do we translate into existing GitHub-shaped types (least churn, risk of semantic drift — e.g. no token expiry, no auto-merge API) or introduce provider-tagged PR detail types? Note CLAUDE.md's rule against `ApiFoo` adapter-smell types cuts both ways here.
6. **Webhooks.** Forgejo/Gitea webhooks use different payload shapes ("gitea" event type) and signature headers (needs verification: `X-Gitea-Signature` vs `X-Hub-Signature-256`, which Forgejo also supports for "github"-type webhooks). New route `/api/v1/webhooks/forgejo`? Separate secret? Does the automation materializer understand both event grammars? Is the Tailscale-funnel/server-URL webhook strategy reused?
7. **OAuth login.** Is "sign in with your Forgejo account" (a *self-hosted* IdP — issuer/allowed-hosts config, trust questions, `AuthMethod`/`IdpIdentity` changes) part of this, or out of scope? Two reasonable answers.
8. **Multi-tenancy.** GitHub is a single global counterparty; Forgejo is many instances. Support exactly one configured instance, or several simultaneously (per-run origin decides)? Changes settings schema, vault keys (`FORGEJO_TOKEN`? per-instance?), and slug identity (owner/repo is no longer unique without the instance).
9. **Non-goals / adjacent providers.** Should the design generalize to Gitea itself (Forgejo is Gitea-compatible; codeberg.org is Forgejo) from day one, or hard-scope to Forgejo branding? `is_github_origin`-style host matching would then be wrong for one of them.

Everything else can follow from those four decisions.

## 2. Goal restated, concretely

> Let Fabro operate against a **self-hosted Forgejo instance** (a Gitea fork; API at `<instance>/api/v1`) the way it operates against GitHub today: a user can configure Forgejo credentials in settings/vault, run workflows whose git origin points at the Forgejo instance (clone-based Docker/Daytona sandboxes accept it), get per-run tokens injected, have runs open/merge/close pull requests on Forgejo, optionally receive Forgejo webhooks to trigger automations, and manage connection status/diagnostics from the web UI — with docs and tests mirroring `docs/public/integrations/github.mdx` and `test/twin/github`.

Forgejo platform facts I verified against current docs: API base is `<instance>/api/v1` (self-hosted, must be configurable); auth is PAT (`Authorization: token ...`), OAuth2 tokens (`Bearer ...`), or basic auth — **there is no GitHub-App-style RS256-JWT → installation-token endpoint**; "Authorized Integrations" (JWT/OIDC, JWKS-validated) exist but target CI-issued tokens, not a hosted server minting scoped tokens. REST endpoints are Gitea-shaped (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`, merge via `POST .../pulls/{index}/merge` with `Do` field) — *not* byte-identical to GitHub (different paths, methods, payload field names, pagination).

## 3. What I now know for certain

- The integration is **deep and load-bearing**: `fabro-github` has 6 dependent crates; origin parsing, run admission, sandbox cloning, PR lifecycle, token minting/refresh (with provenance and replication-lag retry), webhooks, OAuth login, install wizard, diagnostics, and system-integration status are all GitHub-specific today.
- There is an **existing seam for multi-SCM**: `RunScmSettings { provider: Option<String>, owner, repository, github: Option<ScmGitHubSettings> }` in run settings (also in the OpenAPI spec), and `RepositoryProvider::{Github, Git, Unknown}` — i.e., the codebase already anticipates named SCM providers even though everything below it assumes GitHub.
- `GITHUB_BASE_URL` env override already exists in `fabro-github::github_api_base_url()` (used by tests/diagnostics) — but the URL grammar (`parse_github_owner_repo`) is hard-coded to `github.com` hostnames, so it alone can't target a Forgejo instance.
- Clone-based providers (Docker, Daytona) **explicitly reject non-GitHub origins** (`clone_source.rs` error message; CLAUDE.md documents "GitHub-only clone-source contract"). Daytona clones via its SDK with `owner/repo` + GitHub credentials.
- Secrets flow: vault-backed (`fabro-install` writes `GITHUB_*` keys), with a registry of secret env names (`fabro-static/src/secret_registry.rs`) and scrubbing policy.
- The test architecture expects a **twin server** per external dependency (`test/twin/openai`, `test/twin/github` with fixture-driven handlers + git smart-HTTP), and strategy docs (`docs/internal/`) constrain events, errors, testing, secrets, migrations, and API type ownership — all apply to this feature.
- Auth model: browser login via GitHub OAuth (`ServerAuthMethod::Github`, `github_endpoints.rs`, `/login/oauth/*` + `/user`), distinct from the repo-integration credential strategy (`token` vs `app`).
- Webhook ingestion is one route (`/api/v1/webhooks/github`) authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 `X-Hub-Signature-256`, feeding automations via `automation_materializer.rs`.
- Forgejo specifics (from official docs, v16): `/api/v1` base, `token`/`Bearer`/basic auth, OAuth2 provider present, pagination `page`/`limit`, OpenAPI published at `/swagger.v1.json`; no installation-token equivalent.

1. **Scope of parity.** Full GitHub parity (clone, run token, PRs, webhooks, OAuth login, tracker, install wizard, diagnostics) vs. the pragmatic core (PAT auth + clone + PR lifecycle)? "Similar to github integration" doesn't say. GitHub Projects V2 tracker almost certainly has **no Forgejo equivalent** (Gitea/Forgejo projects lack a public GraphQL API).
2. **Auth model mapping.** GitHub has App (JWT → scoped installation tokens, the basis of `GITHUB_TOKEN` minting and `token_source.rs` refresh logic) vs. PAT. Forgejo only has PAT/OAuth2. Do we: (a) support only a static PAT (simplest; kills the per-run scoped-token feature), (b) map to Forgejo OAuth2 tokens, or (c) attempt "Authorized Integrations" JWT (JWKS-hosting required — Fabro would have to run an OIDC issuer, a big new surface)?
3. **Instance URL model.** One Forgejo instance configured globally (server-level, like `[server.integrations.forgejo] url = "..."`), or resolved per-repo-origin (any host that isn't github.com)? And how do run origins get classified — does `RepositoryProvider` grow a `Forgejo` variant, and is that by configured-instance match or URL heuristics? Affects `GitHubRepositorySlug`, `PullRequestLink` (currently hard-coded to `github.com` URLs), DB-stored data, and the API schema.
4. **Architecture: sibling crate vs. provider abstraction.** A `fabro-forgejo` crate next to `fabro-github` (fast, parallel, but duplicates and pushes `if provider == …` branching into server/workflow/sandbox), vs. extracting a `ForgeProvider` trait (e.g. parse origin / resolve clone creds / create PR / merge PR) that both implement — a large refactor of `fabro-github`'s public surface (`GitHubContext`, `GitHubRepositoryAccess`, `InstallationTokenSource`) that touches every dependent crate. Also: does `token_source.rs`'s refresh/provenance machinery get reused for static Forgejo PATs (it already has a `Static` provenance) or forked?
5. **API-shape translation.** Gitea-family REST differs in details (merge endpoint method/fields like `Do`, token header `token` vs `Bearer`, pagination, PR JSON schema differences feeding `PullRequestGithubDetail`). Do we translate into existing GitHub-shaped types (least churn, risk of semantic drift — e.g. no token expiry, no auto-merge API) or introduce provider-tagged PR detail types? Note CLAUDE.md's rule against `ApiFoo` adapter-smell types cuts both ways here.
6. **Webhooks.** Forgejo/Gitea webhooks use different payload shapes ("gitea" event type) and signature headers (needs verification: `X-Gitea-Signature` vs `X-Hub-Signature-256`, which Forgejo also supports for "github"-type webhooks). New route `/api/v1/webhooks/forgejo`? Separate secret? Does the automation materializer understand both event grammars? Is the Tailscale-funnel/server-URL webhook strategy reused?
7. **OAuth login.** Is "sign in with your Forgejo account" (a *self-hosted* IdP — issuer/allowed-hosts config, trust questions, `AuthMethod`/`IdpIdentity` changes) part of this, or out of scope? Two reasonable answers.
8. **Multi-tenancy.** GitHub is a single global counterparty; Forgejo is many instances. Support exactly one configured instance, or several simultaneously (per-run origin decides)? Changes settings schema, vault keys (`FORGEJO_TOKEN`? per-instance?), and slug identity (owner/repo is no longer unique without the instance).
9. **Non-goals / adjacent providers.** Should the design generalize to Gitea itself (Forgejo is Gitea-compatible; codeberg.org is Forgejo) from day one, or hard-scope to Forgejo branding? `is_github_origin`-style host matching would then be wrong for one of them.
10. **Product surfaces.** Does the web install wizard, `fabro install forgejo` CLI, system integrations status card (`IntegrationProvider::Forgejo`), and OpenAPI/TS client updates all land in phase one, or is this a CLI/server-only feature initially? (The OpenAPI-first workflow makes each schema change ripple into conformance tests and the generated TS client.)

**Recommended clarifications before building:** (1) target scope (clone+PR core vs. full parity), (2) PAT-only auth for v1, (3) single configured instance vs. per-origin detection, (4) sibling crate with a thin shared trait vs. full provider abstraction. Everything else can follow from those four decisions.

## 2. Goal restated, concretely

> Let Fabro operate against a **self-hosted Forgejo instance** (a Gitea fork; API at `<instance>/api/v1`) the way it operates against GitHub today: a user can configure Forgejo credentials in settings/vault, run workflows whose git origin points at the Forgejo instance (clone-based Docker/Daytona sandboxes accept it), get per-run tokens injected, have runs open/merge/close pull requests on Forgejo, optionally receive Forgejo webhooks to trigger automations, and manage connection status/diagnostics from the web UI — with docs and tests mirroring `docs/public/integrations/github.mdx` and `test/twin/github`.

Forgejo platform facts I verified against current docs: API base is `<instance>/api/v1` (self-hosted, must be configurable); auth is PAT (`Authorization: token ...`), OAuth2 tokens (`Bearer ...`), or basic auth — **there is no GitHub-App-style RS256-JWT → installation-token endpoint**; "Authorized Integrations" (JWT/OIDC, JWKS-validated) exist but target CI-issued tokens, not a hosted server minting scoped tokens. REST endpoints are Gitea-shaped (`/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls`, merge via `POST .../pulls/{index}/merge` with `Do` field) — *not* byte-identical to GitHub (different paths, methods, payload field names, pagination).

## 3. What I now know for certain

- The integration is **deep and load-bearing**: `fabro-github` has 6 dependent crates; origin parsing, run admission, sandbox cloning, PR lifecycle, token minting/refresh (with provenance and replication-lag retry), webhooks, OAuth login, install wizard, diagnostics, and system-integration status are all GitHub-specific today.
- There is an **existing seam for multi-SCM**: `RunScmSettings { provider: Option<String>, owner, repository, github: Option<ScmGitHubSettings> }` in run settings (also in the OpenAPI spec), and `RepositoryProvider::{Github, Git, Unknown}` — i.e., the codebase already anticipates named SCM providers even though everything below it assumes GitHub.
- `GITHUB_BASE_URL` env override already exists in `fabro-github::github_api_base_url()` (used by tests/diagnostics) — but the URL grammar (`parse_github_owner_repo`) is hard-coded to `github.com` hostnames, so it alone can't target a Forgejo instance.
- Clone-based providers (Docker, Daytona) **explicitly reject non-GitHub origins** (`clone_source.rs` error message; CLAUDE.md documents "GitHub-only clone-source contract"). Daytona clones via its SDK with `owner/repo` + GitHub credentials.
- Secrets flow: vault-backed (`fabro-install` writes `GITHUB_*` keys), with a registry of secret env names (`fabro-static/src/secret_registry.rs`) and scrubbing policy.
- The test architecture expects a **twin server** per external dependency (`test/twin/openai`, `test/twin/github` with fixture-driven handlers + git smart-HTTP), and strategy docs (`docs/internal/`) constrain events, errors, testing, secrets, migrations, and API type ownership — all apply to this feature.
- Auth model: browser login via GitHub OAuth (`ServerAuthMethod::Github`, `github_endpoints.rs`, `/login/oauth/*` + `/user`), distinct from the repo-integration credential strategy (`token` vs `app`).
- Webhook ingestion is one route (`/api/v1/webhooks/github`) authenticated by HMAC-SHA256 `X-Hub-Signature-256`, feeding automations via `automation_materializer.rs`.
- Forgejo specifics (from official docs, v16): `/api/v1` base, `token`/`Bearer`/basic auth, OAuth2 provider present, pagination `page`/`limit`, OpenAPI published at `/swagger.v1.json`; no installation-token equivalent.

## 4. Genuinely ambiguous — where two engineers would build different things

1. **Scope of parity.** Full GitHub parity (clone, run token, PRs, webhooks, OAuth login, tracker, install wizard, diagnostics) vs. the pragmatic core (PAT auth + clone + PR lifecycle)? "Similar to github integration" doesn't say. GitHub Projects V2 tracker almost certainly has **no Forgejo equivalent** (Gitea/Forgejo projects lack a public GraphQL API).
2. **Auth model mapping.** GitHub has App (JWT → scoped installation tokens, the basis of `GITHUB_TOKEN` minting and `token_source.rs` refresh logic) vs. PAT. Forgejo only has PAT/OAuth2. Do we: (a) support only a static PAT (simplest; kills the per-run scoped-token feature), (b) map to Forgejo OAuth2 tokens, or (c) attempt "Authorized Integrations" JWT (JWKS-hosting required — Fabro would have to run an OIDC issuer, a big new surface)?
3. **Instance URL model.** One Forgejo instance configured globally (server-level, like `[server.integrations.forgejo] url = "..."`), or resolved per-repo-origin (any host that isn't github.com)? And how do run origins get classified — does `RepositoryProvider` grow a `Forgejo` variant, and is that by configured-instance match or URL heuristics? Affects `GitHubRepositorySlug`, `PullRequestLink` (currently hard-coded to `github.com` URLs), DB-stored data, and the API schema.
4. **Architecture: sibling crate vs. provider abstraction.** A `fabro-forgejo` crate next to `fabro-github` (fast, parallel, but duplicates and pushes `if provider == …` branching into server/workflow/sandbox), vs. extracting a `ForgeProvider` trait (e.g. parse origin / resolve clone creds / create PR / merge PR) that both implement — a large refactor of `fabro-github`'s public surface (`GitHubContext`, `GitHubRepositoryAccess`, `InstallationTokenSource`) that touches every dependent crate. Also: does `token_source.rs`'s refresh/provenance machinery get reused for static Forgejo PATs (it already has a `Static` provenance) or forked?
5. **API-shape translation.** Gitea-family REST differs in details (merge endpoint method/fields like `Do`, token header `token` vs `Bearer`, pagination, PR JSON schema differences feeding `PullRequestGithubDetail`). Do we translate into existing GitHub-shaped types (least churn, risk of semantic drift — e.g. no token expiry, no auto-merge API) or introduce provider-tagged PR detail types? Note CLAUDE.md's rule against `ApiFoo` adapter-smell types cuts both ways here.
6. **Webhooks.** Forgejo/Gitea webhooks use different payload shapes ("gitea" event type) and signature headers (needs verification: `X-Gitea-Signature` vs `X-Hub-Signature-256`, which Forgejo also supports for "github"-type webhooks). New route `/api/v1/webhooks/forgejo`? Separate secret? Does the automation materializer understand both event grammars? Is the Tailscale-funnel/server-URL webhook strategy reused?
7. **OAuth login.** Is "sign in with your Forgejo account" (a *self-hosted* IdP — issuer/allowed-hosts config, trust questions, `AuthMethod`/`IdpIdentity` changes) part of this, or out of scope? Two reasonable answers.
8. **Multi-tenancy.** GitHub is a single global counterparty; Forgejo is many instances. Support exactly one configured instance, or several simultaneously (per-run origin decides)? Changes settings schema, vault keys (`FORGEJO_TOKEN`? per-instance?), and slug identity (owner/repo is no longer unique without the instance).
9. **Non-goals / adjacent providers.** Should the design generalize to Gitea itself (Forgejo is Gitea-compatible; codeberg.org is Forgejo) from day one, or hard-scope to Forgejo branding? `is_github_origin`-style host matching would then be wrong for one of them.
10. **Product surfaces.** Does the web install wizard, `fabro install forgejo` CLI, system integrations status card (`IntegrationProvider::Forgejo`), and OpenAPI/TS client updates all land in phase one, or is this a CLI/server-only feature initially? (The OpenAPI-first workflow makes each schema change ripple into conformance tests and the generated TS client.)

**Recommended clarifications before building:** (1) target scope (clone+PR core vs. full parity), (2) PAT-only auth for v1, (3) single configured instance vs. per-origin detection, (4) sibling crate with a thin shared trait vs. full provider abstraction. Everything else can follow from those four decisions.

## Order

1 → 2 → 3 → 4 → 5 → 6 → 7 → 8, with `cargo nextest run -p <touched crate>` after each phase. Phase 4's event-host work lands **before** Phase 5's dispatch tests so the projection carries host when the server tests exercise it. OpenAPI (7) is after handlers exist because the wire shape settles then.

## Verification

- Per-crate nextest for every touched crate (`fabro-forgejo`, `fabro-static`, `fabro-types`, `fabro-config`, `fabro-sandbox`, `fabro-workflow`, `fabro-store`, `fabro-server`, `fabro-cli`, `fabro-manifest`, `fabro-install`).
- The critique-regression test: `Event → RunEvent → run_state projection` round-trip keeps `host`; server merge test uses the twin forgejo, proving dispatch is not silently hitting `api.github.com` (a wrong dispatch fails here, not in production).
- API regen: `cargo build -p fabro-api`; `fabro-server` conformance test (spec/router drift).
- TS: `bun run generate` in `lib/packages/fabro-api-client`, then `cd apps/fabro-web && bun run typecheck && bun test`.
- Snapshots: `cargo insta pending-snapshots`, review, targeted `cargo insta accept`.
- Full gate: `cargo build --workspace`; `cargo nextest run --workspace`; `cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 fmt --check --all`; `cargo +nightly-2026-04-14 clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`; e2e twin profile for the new tests, then full e2e profile.
- Manual one-time smoke (documented in PR): official Forgejo docker image — `fabro install forgejo --url … --token …`, run in a repo whose `origin` points at it, verify the PR URL opens on the instance (`/pulls/N`), merge via the `fabro pr` flow. Only a real Gitea git-over-HTTPS server proves the twin can't.

## Deliberately not doing

- Webhooks/automations, browser OAuth login, tracker — out of scope (scope answer); `github_webhooks.rs`, `auth/github_endpoints.rs`, `fabro-tracker` untouched.
- Provider-trait refactor of `fabro-github` — sibling crate per architecture answer.
- Multi-instance / auto-detection — single configured instance; `PullRequestLink.host` keeps per-record hosts so a later map is additive, not a schema break.
- Daytona Forgejo clones — SDK clone is GitHub-shaped; explicit admission error, documented.
- API/RunIntent git targets for Forgejo — `GitRunTarget.repo` is a host-ambiguous GitHub slug; changing that grammar is a wire break out of scope. Forgejo runs originate from a workspace git remote.
- Auto-merge on Forgejo — no API; explicit `PullRequestFailed` error.
- Per-run scoped minting / `[run.integrations.forgejo]` — PAT-only; scopes live on the Forgejo token; PAT forwarded verbatim as `FORGEJO_TOKEN`.
- `RepositoryProvider::Forgejo` — needs configured host in config-free `fabro-types`; forgejo origins stay `Git` in display metadata.
- `spawn_env.rs` changes — verified unnecessary (vault-based flow).
- Web wizard/settings-card UI — lean reading of the last answer; only the system-integrations *endpoint* grows a forgejo entry.

agent_tools.name: close_agent
agent_tools.description: Close a running or completed subagent that is no longer needed.

agent_tools.name: edit_file
agent_tools.description: Edit a file by replacing an exact string. The old_string must be an exact match and unique unless replace_all is true; include surrounding context when needed. Read the file first and preserve existing indentation.

agent_tools.name: glob
agent_tools.description: Find files by search-root-relative path using a glob pattern. Use path to choose the search root. `*` stays within one path segment and `**` searches recursively. Prefer this over shell find or ls when locating repository files.

agent_tools.name: grep
agent_tools.description: Search file contents with a regex pattern. Use path to choose the search root, glob_filter to limit matching files, case_insensitive for case folding, and max_results to cap output.

agent_tools.name: read_file
agent_tools.description: Read files before editing them. Returns line-numbered text and supports offset/limit for large files. Use this instead of shell cat, head, tail, or sed when inspecting repository files.

agent_tools.name: request_user_input
agent_tools.description: Ask the human one or more questions and wait for their answers before continuing this stage.

agent_tools.name: send_input
agent_tools.description: Send a follow-up message to a subagent. A running agent receives it at a safe turn boundary. A completed agent starts another turn in the same session with its existing history.

agent_tools.name: shell
agent_tools.description: Execute Bash commands for terminal operations, package managers, tests and builds. Use dedicated tools for file reads, file edits, filename searches, and content searches. Provide timeout_ms for long-running commands.

agent_tools.name: spawn_agent
agent_tools.description: Spawn a subagent for independent work or context isolation. Use it for tasks that can proceed separately, and avoid duplicating the same work in the parent session.

agent_tools.name: update_plan
agent_tools.description: Update the multi-step plan for the current task. Submit the entire plan; existing steps are reconciled by exact step text.

agent_tools.name: use_skill
agent_tools.description: Load a skill's instructions by name. Call this when the user's request matches an available skill.

agent_tools.name: wait
agent_tools.description: Wait for a subagent to complete, then use the result to synthesize the outcome for the user.

agent_tools.name: web_fetch
agent_tools.description: Fetch content from a URL that starts with http:// or https://. Pass a prompt to extract specific information or summarize the page; omit prompt to return the page content.

agent_tools.name: write_file
agent_tools.description: Create new files, or overwrite an existing file only when replacement is explicitly intended. Prefer edit_file for targeted changes to existing files because write_file overwrites the full file content.
